content.value_statement: AI features can fail from weak prompts, poor retrieval, latency, and cost surprises. This skill gives production patterns for LLM integration, RAG, validation, monitoring, and fallback design.
actual_capabilities: Explains structured LLM output with schema validation.
Shows streaming response patterns for user-facing AI features.
Describes RAG retrieval with semantic search, keyword search, reranking, and context limits.
Covers prompt versioning, prompt testing, and A/B testing practices.
Outlines cost tracking, usage limits, provider fallbacks, and circuit breakers.
Lists validation checks for common LLM product risks.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a complete application framework.
It does not validate your live model behavior or production data.
It does not replace security, legal, or domain expert review for high-stakes AI features.
It assumes the user can adapt TypeScript-style examples to their stack.

use_cases.title: Plan an AI feature launch
use_cases.description: Use the patterns to define validation, streaming, fallbacks, cost tracking, and success metrics before implementation.

use_cases.title: Design a RAG workflow
use_cases.description: Apply hybrid search, reranking, context budgeting, and source verification to a document-based assistant.

use_cases.title: Harden an existing LLM integration
use_cases.description: Review prompt injection defenses, schema validation, timeout handling, provider fallback, and monitoring gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Map a first AI feature
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new AI product capability.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan an AI feature for this product: [product]. Identify the user workflow, LLM role, required data, validation needs, fallback behavior, and cost risks.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a prompt safely
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt review before production use.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this production prompt: [prompt]. Find injection risks, missing constraints, unclear output expectations, testing gaps, and versioning needs.

prompt_templates.title: Design a RAG system
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced architecture for retrieval-based AI features.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a RAG architecture for [knowledge source] and [user task]. Include chunking, embedding, keyword search, reranking, context limits, source verification, and update strategy.

prompt_templates.title: Audit production AI reliability
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a deployed LLM workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this AI workflow: [workflow details]. Assess validation, prompt injection defenses, latency, streaming, cost tracking, rate limits, provider fallback, monitoring, and human review boundaries.

output_examples.input: Plan a support ticket classifier that uses an LLM.
output: Recommended design: structured output with schema validation, prompt versioning, and regression tests.
Operational controls: usage logging, per-user limits, fallback categories, and review for low-confidence cases.
User experience: show clear category results and allow correction for future evaluation.

output_examples.input: Review a RAG assistant for customer documentation.
output: Retrieval plan: combine semantic search, keyword search, reranking, and strict context budgeting.
Trust controls: cite sources, verify source availability, show uncertainty, and avoid unsupported claims.
Reliability controls: cache common queries, monitor token spend, and handle provider failures gracefully.

output_examples.input: Harden a chat feature before launch.
output: Security gaps: separate user input from system instructions and filter likely injection attempts.
Product gaps: stream responses, use progress states, and define fallback behavior for outages.
Measurement gaps: track latency, tokens, cost per request, errors, and user correction rates.

best_practices: Validate every LLM response before using it in application logic.
Version prompts and test them with representative regression cases.
Track latency, token usage, cost, errors, and fallback behavior from launch.
anti_patterns: Putting raw user input directly into privileged prompt instructions.
Using RAG without context limits, source verification, or relevance ranking.
Shipping LLM calls without timeouts, rate limits, fallback paths, or cost alerts.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you design production AI product features that use LLMs, RAG, prompt testing, streaming UX, and cost controls.

faq.question: Does this skill write a complete application?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture patterns, review checklists, and implementation guidance that you adapt to your codebase.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it cover prompt injection?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how prompt injection happens and recommends input separation, sanitization, output filtering, and limited tool access.

faq.question: Does it recommend RAG or fine-tuning first?
faq.answer: It recommends RAG and prompt improvements first for most knowledge workflows. Fine-tuning is presented as a later option with clear requirements.

faq.question: Is it suitable for high-stakes domains?
faq.answer: It can support planning, but high-stakes medical, legal, financial, or safety use cases still need expert review and domain validation.
